subject: general
question: "Raid" is a commonly used term in which Indian sport?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kabaddi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Raid** is the primary offensive move in the sport of **Kabaddi**, where a single player from the attacking team, known as the **raider**, runs into the opposing team's half of the court.
 
• The **raider** must continuously chant the word "**Kabaddi**" throughout the duration of the attack without inhaling; this rhythmic chanting is technically referred to as the **cant**.
 
• In professional formats like the **Pro Kabaddi League (PKL)**, which was launched in **2014**, each **raid** is restricted to a maximum time limit of **30 seconds**.
 
• The objective of a **raid** is to tag or touch one or more members of the defending team and return safely to the home half. Successfully doing so earns the attacking team **touch points**, while failure to return results in the **raider** being declared "out."
 
• **Kabaddi** is a contact sport with deep roots in **ancient India**, particularly in the state of **Tamil Nadu**. It gained massive international exposure after its introduction as a competitive sport in the **1990 Asian Games** held in **Beijing**.
 
• The sport is governed globally by the **International Kabaddi Federation (IKF)** and in India by the **Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI)**, which was established in **1972**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cricket**:

 
 
• This is a bat-and-ball game played between two teams of **11 players** each.
 
• Commonly used terms include **LBW (Leg Before Wicket)**, **Maiden Over**, **Yorker**, **Duck**, **Silley Point**, and **Powerplay**.
 
• The **International Cricket Council (ICC)**, headquartered in **Dubai**, is the global governing body.
 
 
 
• **Football**:
 
 
• Known as soccer in some regions, it is a sport where two teams of **11 players** use their feet to propel a ball into the opposing goal.
 
• Key terminologies include **Offside**, **Dribbling**, **Free Kick**, **Yellow Card**, **Corner Kick**, and **VAR (Video Assistant Referee)**.
 
• The **FIFA World Cup**, held every **four years**, is the most prestigious tournament in this sport.
 
 
 
• **Hockey**:
 
 
• Field hockey is a widely popular sport in **India** and was historically considered the **national sport** of the country.
 
• Important terms include **Bully**, **Short Corner**, **Penalty Stroke**, **Dribble**, and **Scoop**.
 
• India has won a record **eight Olympic gold medals** in men's hockey, with legends like **Major Dhyan Chand** contributing to its golden era.
 
 
 
• **Other Indian Sports**:
 
 
• **Kho-Kho**: Another traditional Indian tag sport involving terms like **Chaser**, **Active Chaser**, and **Runner**.
 
• **Mallakhamba**: A traditional Indian sport in which a gymnast performs aerial yoga or gymnastics postures and wrestling grips in concert with a vertical stationary or hanging wooden pole.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In **Kabaddi**, a special rule called the **Do-or-Die Raid** occurs when a team has two consecutive **empty raids** (raids where no points are scored). The third raid becomes mandatory for scoring, or the **raider** is automatically out.
 
• The term **Super Tackle** refers to a situation where a defending team with **three or fewer players** successfully pins down a **raider**, earning **2 points** instead of 1.
 
• The **Lona** is an additional **2 points** awarded to a team when they manage to put the entire opposing team "out."
